stimuli.source: V1 web appendix SOT-1 REBUILT per new plan geometry (the geometry rules (Web Appendix B) SOT rule); see flags.

flags.rebuilt_reason: V1 SOT-1 added a MIDDLE option (3TB/$59.99) between HF and HD, making HD the top extreme. The new plan requires the OPPOSITE geometry: add one NEW EXTREME beyond HD so that HD becomes the middle/compromise. New extreme option is 6TB/$119.99, making HD (4TB/$79.99) the middle option. Statistic is HD/(HD+HF) relative share (excluding the new extreme choosers). V1's middle-insertion geometry would have tested compromise with the wrong option as the compromise target.

stimuli.notes: HD (4TB/$79.99) is now geometrically the middle/compromise between HF (2TB/$39.99) and the extreme (6TB/$119.99). Price spacing: $39.99, $79.99, $119.99 (approximately equal gaps of $40). Storage spacing: 2TB, 4TB, 6TB (equal gaps). The extreme (6TB/$119.99) is beyond the HD option on both attributes.

stimuli.source: Constructed minimally from BIN anchor; no published analog.

flags.construction_rationale: SIM is a new structure (not in V1; no published hard-drive analog exists). Clone is a near-duplicate of HD: same is_hd=true, similar storage (4.5TB vs 4TB, +0.5TB), minimal price distance ($84.99 vs $79.99, +$5.00). A pure 4TB/$84.99 clone would be dominated by HD on price (same storage, higher price). To satisfy the validator rules (stimuli/validate_stimuli.py) non-dominance assertion, the clone must be slightly better on at least one attribute relative to HD: 4.5TB > 4TB satisfies this (clone beats HD on storage; HD beats clone on price - neither dominates). Clone is not dominated by HF (4.5TB >> 2TB). Minimal distance satisfied: the clone is the closest non-dominated option to HD.

stimuli.notes: Clone (4.5TB/$84.99): is_hd=true (same tier as HD). More storage than HD (+0.5TB); higher price (+$5.00). HD does NOT dominate clone (clone beats HD on storage). Clone does NOT dominate HD (HD beats clone on price). Clone is not dominated by HF (4.5TB >> 2TB). Similarity effect prediction: clone steals disproportionate share from HD (the option it most resembles), HF gains relative share vs matched BIN. Non-dominance assertion (the validator rules (stimuli/validate_stimuli.py)) satisfied.
